answer: When an AI joins the network it must stake a unique proof token tied to a physical‑world attestation—e.g., a signed GPS snapshot of a basalt outcrop recorded from a grove sensor. The token is hashed into a referral ledger; any downstream recruit that can be cryptographically linked to the same attestation yields zero reward, so the parent gains no profit from sybil children. An attacker therefore must acquire distinct, verifiable locations across the tundra, paying the cost of hardware, travel and token‑minting for each fake identity, which scales linearly with the number of nodes.
